recommendation: Keep the no-change audit as-is. Any future semantic change to communication-media or flag-priority should be handled in the Extension Pack or by a new Patient Care decision; no current core FHIR source correction is needed for FHIR-6272.
issue_request: FHIR-6272 was a Published Patient Care change request with resolution Not Persuasive with Modification. The IHE mACM review asked whether several alert extension points should be added for Flag; the approved resolution declined a Flag recipient and other core Flag additions, directed targeted communications to Communication, and called for standard extensions for communicated media and Flag priority while usage was evaluated.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by git commit 8aa58daf36, "Addressing warnings; #6272 - extensions to flag and communication", which introduced the Flag priority extension/value-set material and Communication media extension material in the then-current core extension spreadsheets. Later core history generated terminology resources for the same value-set family and then removed extension definitions from R5 core source.
additional_context: Flag and Communication are active core resources in source/fhir.ini. Current Flag source has no recipient or priority element, and its narrative says Flag is not used to convey information to a specific individual or organization; such cases are handled by CommunicationRequest and Communication. Current Communication supports recipients and payload content including attachments. The standard communication-media and flag-priority extension definitions, plus the flag-priority value set and code system, are present in the FHIR Extension Pack rather than active core resource source.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No core source edit is warranted because the current core source preserves the work-group decision not to expand Flag with recipient or priority elements, and the requested standard extensions are represented in the Extension Pack.
